jobs.description:
Description

About The Port Authority:

Founded in 1921, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey builds, operates, and maintains many of the most important transportation and trade infrastructure assets in the country. The agency's network of aviation, ground, rail, and seaport facilities is among the busiest in the country, supports more than 550,000 regional jobs, and generates more than twenty three billion in annual wages and eighty billion in annual economic activity. The Port Authority also owns and manages the 16-acre World Trade Center site, where the 1,776-foot-tall One World Trade Center is now the tallest skyscraper in the Western Hemisphere.

About The Port Department

The Port Department is one of the five-line department businesses of the PANYNJ. It is responsible for managing the largest port complex on the East Coast and the second largest in the nation. It operates a highly competitive and dynamic business in a very complex political environment. The Port is an economic engine that provides over 580,000 jobs in the region and nearly $240 billion in annual economic activity.

For the past 20 years, the Port has been preparing itself for the growing demand for increased trade resulting in more cargo and for the rapid migration to ever larger vessels. Together with our Port tenants, nearly $15 billion in new infrastructure, equipment and systems has been invested to ensure that Port of New York and New Jersey remains the premier East Coast gateway with even more investment in capacity planned and underway.

As a landlord Port, the Port Authority leases property to tenants that operate Port facilities. Since we do not directly handle cargo, we must influence the efficiency and productivity of the port in more strategic ways. Today, the challenges in this area continue to grow. Improving Port productivity requires a more collaborative approach. The Port Department has taken a strong leadership role in driving the changes necessary to keep the Port of New York and New Jersey highly competitive while ensuring growth in a safe, secure, sustainable and resilient way.

The Port Authority is a unique government body serving both the States of New York and New Jersey, mandated to be financially self-sufficient. As such, increasing revenues while remaining competitive is a major challenge for the Port Department moving forward.

Functional Oversight

Reporting to the Director of the Port Department, the Deputy Port Director
is a member of the senior management team of the Port Department and is responsible for oversight of the Department’s facilities, business services, commercial development, planning and capital program delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Represent the Director in all matters related to managing the Port Department, as needed.
Oversee and provide direction to the Departmental leadership that manages and directs all aspects of facility operations, maintenance, regulatory compliance (safety, security, environmental), commercial development, business services, planning and capital project delivery, while providing for meaningful and measurable improvements in how we serve the global supply chain, deliver critical infrastructure improvements, and support the communities in which we operate.
Provide strategic guidance on the development and implementation of procedures to protect existing revenue, generate new revenue sources and obtain maximum productivity/capacity of the Port facilities, control expenditures and ensuring that the department generates the maximum net contribution to the Agency.
Provide oversight, leadership, and guidance to matters associated with advancing initiatives that require inter-departmental cooperation. Work with other departments to reach consensus about roles and responsibilities, with a focus on the impact that decisions have on operations, maintenance, capital investment, sustainability, and customer service activities.
Participate in the development of the department’s strategic planning and policy agenda, business plan and support initiatives that increase revenue, reduce costs, and improve process efficiency, port efficiency, capacity, and customer service.
Provide strategic direction to all aspects of the Department’s asset management programs, including capital and operating project delivery, maintenance management and tenant support services.
Continuously review the department’s organizational structure and functions to ensure effective, efficient staff alignments that satisfy the department’s mission and vision, while supporting a work climate that embraces diversity and inclusion. Work with department leaders, to ensure staff capability, availability, competence, and motivation.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business administration, Transportation, International Trade, Logistics, Engineering or a related field from an accredited college or university. A graduate degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Transportation, Engineering, or a related field is preferred.
Minimum of 20 years of progressively responsible experience at an executive level capacity, preferably working for an organization comparable to the size and complexity of the operation in the Port of New York and New Jersey, with at least 10 years in the port and maritime transportation arena.
Must possess a valid Driver’s License and be able to obtain a Transportation Worker’s Identification Credential (TWIC) within 60 days of assuming the position.

The Ideal Candidate Will Present The Following Profile

At least 15 years of progressively responsible operations, planning, project management, customer service, performance management, property maintenance, and infrastructure management experience in a complex transportation environment.
At least 5 years of progressive responsibilities managing and directing the delivery of a broad program portfolio, measuring and improving implementation, recommending and advocating policy changes, evaluating and implementing alternate project delivery systems, and establishing and meeting Agency and Department level performance measures.
Extensive knowledge of the global supply chain and the port and maritime transportation system.
Demonstrated senior level experience in managing, leading, mentoring and developing a large diverse staff, with a proven record of effective team building and providing for successful outcomes.
Demonstrated experience in complex negotiations and conflict resolution supported by strong transactional, analytical and decision-making skills.
Superior interpersonal skills interacting with internal staff at all levels, and a broad range of external stakeholders such as government agencies, elected officials, community organizations, tenants, trade associations, contractors, consultants, and regional transportation organizations.
Demonstrated experience interacting and navigating a complex organization.
Demonstrated ability to manage conflict, build consensus, and facilitate problem solving and collaboration among various stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability developing strategies to achieve broad business goals and to understand the impact on various stakeholders/constituents within and outside of the PA.
Superior written and oral communication skills with demonstrated experience in preparing and delivering presentation materials to a broad executive and senior staff, and both internal and external stakeholders.

Compensation, Benefits & On-Site Collaboration Requirements

In accordance with Port Authority policy, this position permits employees to work remotely a maximum of one day per week. In person collaboration is essential to how the Port Authority conducts business, and regular in-office days or team collaboration days may be required on business needs.

jobs.description:
Waller Consulting post, on behalf of East Coopera Community Outreach

Lead the Next Chapter of Neighbors Helping Neighbors

In 1989, Hurricane Hugo tore through the Lowcountry, and a handful of neighbors turned a parish hall into a lifeline. Thirty-six years later, that same instinct still drives East Cooper Community Outreach (ECCO), a $3.3 million, professionally run nonprofit now serving more than 2,700 individuals a year. After a decade of fast growth, we’re ready to build the fundraising engine and organizational systems to make that growth last. We’re looking for the person who wants to lead that work.

Who We Are 

ECCO provides food, clothing, financial assistance, and dental and medical care to neighbors across Mount Pleasant and East Cooper, paired with coaching and resources (financial workshops, career support, an Asset Development matched-savings program) that help people build lasting stability, not just get through the week. We’ve grown from roughly $500,000 to $3.3 million in annual budget over the last decade, completed a $5.7 million capital campaign, and built a donor base of more than 1,500 people who believe in this work. 
Our culture is the thing people mention first: compassion, collaboration, respect, and integrity, not as a poster on the wall, but as how we actually treat clients, each other, and this community. We’re proud of that, and we’re looking for a CEO who will protect it fiercely while helping us grow.
The Opportunity 

The Board recently elevated this role from Executive Director to CEO, and has built a strong leadership team well positioned to take full responsibility for day-to-day operations, freeing our next CEO to focus on what matters most right now: fundraising, strategy, and building a Board that operates as a true strategic partner. This is a lead-fundraiser role as much as a chief-executive role. Your first job will be strengthening what we’ve already built: stabilizing our development function, deepening donor relationships, and helping our Board grow into stronger governance. From that foundation, you’ll help shape our next 3–5 year strategic plan, including how far and how fast we grow from here. 
Compensation is $128,000 to $160,000, with a comprehensive benefits package including employer-paid health insurance, retirement contributions, and generous paid time off. You’d be doing this work in Mount Pleasant, SC, part of the fast-growing, high-quality-of-life Charleston area. 
A Strong Organization, Ready for What’s Next 

ECCO isn’t a struggling organization looking for someone to rescue it. It’s a 36-year-old institution with real financial momentum (a completed $5.7 million capital campaign, a donor base that keeps growing, three decades of deep community trust), and a culture that clients, staff, and volunteers consistently describe as the best they’ve been part of. That foundation is genuinely rare, and it’s yours to build on, not repair. 
Here’s the honest part: growing organizations outgrow their own systems, and ECCO is right in the middle of that stretch. Our Board is evolving toward stronger strategic governance, our fundraising infrastructure is being built out, and our next CEO will have real influence over how that next chapter takes shape, rather than walking into something already finished. If that sounds like an opportunity instead of a warning sign, keep reading. 
Is This You? 

You’re a real fundraiser.
You’ve personally closed major gifts before, not just supervised someone who did. 
You’re a connector.
You build trust fast with clients, staff, volunteers, donors, and board members alike, and you genuinely like being the face of an organization.
You can manage up.
You know how to set expectations with a board, and you’re energized (not drained) by helping one grow into stronger governance. 
You lead with humility.
Your first instinct in a new role is to listen and learn, not to arrive with a fixed plan; but you’re also ready to lead real change once you’ve earned the trust to do it. 
You’re a builder, not a boss.
You believe in transparent communication, and you want a staff that feels heard, not managed from a distance. 
You think in systems.
You want to help ECCO finish growing up, better systems, better onboarding, better infrastructure, without losing what makes it feel like ECCO. 

The Fine Print

Board of Directors

$128,000 – $160,000, plus a comprehensive benefits package Location
On-site, Mount Pleasant, SC 
Required
Bachelor’s degree; 10+ years of progressive senior leadership experience; a proven track record personally securing major gifts; experience managing 
teams, budgets, and complex operations

Prior Executive Director, CEO, COO, Chief Development Officer, or Director of Development experience; nonprofit or human-services background; strong 
board governance experience; a leadership style rooted in humility, emotional 
intelligence, and resilience 
How to Apply

at info@capacitytodream.com

jobs.description:
Position Summary

Access Health Louisiana (AHL) seeks a senior healthcare operations leader to provide regional leadership for AHL’s Northshore operations. This position is responsible for regional clinic operations, access, productivity, quality, patient experience, financial performance support, community relationships, strategic growth, and value-based care execution across assigned Northshore sites and programs.

The Director of Operations-Northshore serves as the senior regional operating leader and community representative for the assigned service area. The role translates organizational strategy into regional execution, supports site leadership, identifies growth opportunities, and works with clinical, finance, quality, population health, behavioral health, pharmacy, dental, school-based health, and central operations teams to improve performance.

This position should have clearly defined decision rights and accountability for the assigned regional portfolio. Specific sites, service lines, budget authority, and reporting relationships should be finalized before posting.

Assigned Regional Portfolio

Community Health Centers, School-Based Health Centers, and associated service locations within the Northshore region as assigned by AHL leadership.
Behavioral health, dental, pharmacy, specialty, outreach, and population health services operating within the region, as applicable.
A final list of assigned sites, managers, service lines, employee count, provider count, and annual visit volume should be attached or inserted before posting.

Essential Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership and Regional Growth

Develop and execute the Northshore regional operating and growth plan in alignment with AHL’s mission, strategic plan, and financial goals.
Identify opportunities for service expansion, new clinic development, school-based health center growth, specialty integration, pharmacy alignment, behavioral health integration, and community partnerships.
Lead or support feasibility assessments, community needs evaluations, market reviews, and implementation planning for new programs and locations.
Monitor regional healthcare trends, payer developments, population health indicators, competitor activity, and community needs.
Collaborate with executive leadership on innovation, growth, sustainability, and regional positioning.

Operations Management

Provide regional oversight and support for daily operations of assigned Northshore CHCs, SBHCs, and associated service locations.
Hold site leadership accountable for access, productivity, patient flow, staffing, scheduling, patient experience, quality, and financial performance targets.
Lead operational-excellence initiatives focused on appointment access, third-next-available appointment, cycle time, provider template management, staffing optimization, and resource utilization.
Analyze operational dashboards, financial indicators, visit volumes, productivity reports, referral patterns, and access metrics to identify improvement opportunities.
Coordinate corrective action plans when sites or programs fail to meet expected performance standards.
Support compliance with HRSA, FQHC, CMS, state, payer, accreditation, privacy, safety, and organizational requirements in partnership with central compliance and quality resources.

Population Health and Value-Based Care Execution

Serve as the regional champion for population health, value-based care, chronic disease management, preventive care, risk stratification, care coordination, and health-equity strategies.
Use clinical, claims, payer, and registry data to improve quality performance and reduce avoidable utilization.
Drive regional performance on diabetes management, hypertension control, behavioral health integration, preventive screenings, childhood immunizations, women’s health, maternal and infant health, ED utilization, and readmission-related measures.
Work with medical leadership, care management, quality, behavioral health, pharmacy, dental, and central operations teams to implement evidence-based models and close care gaps.
Support achievement of UDS, HEDIS, payer quality, shared-savings, and value-based incentive opportunities.

Quality Improvement and Performance Excellence

Lead continuous quality improvement and operational performance improvement across the region.
Establish a culture of accountability, data-driven management, problem solving, and service excellence.
Review regional quality metrics and coordinate action plans when performance falls below target.
Support NCQA Patient-Centered Medical Home standards, HRSA quality recognition activities, patient safety practices, and patient-experience improvement.
Partner with Medical Affairs and Quality to improve UDS, HEDIS, and payer quality measures.

Community Engagement and External Relations

Serve as AHL’s senior regional representative and community liaison in the Northshore region.
Build and maintain relationships with school districts, hospitals, health systems, behavioral health organizations, community-based organizations, local government, chambers of commerce, faith-based organizations, public health agencies, and economic development entities.
Represent AHL at community events, stakeholder meetings, coalitions, and partnership discussions.
Identify partnerships that improve access, care coordination, community health outcomes, and regional visibility.
Advocate for initiatives that address social drivers of health, access barriers, and regional health disparities.

Financial and Business Performance

Collaborate with Finance and executive leadership to monitor regional operating budgets, revenue, expenses, productivity, and operating performance.
Identify opportunities to improve financial performance while maintaining quality, access, and patient-centered care.
Support grant-funded initiatives, sustainability planning, forecasting, and new-service business planning.
Monitor provider productivity, staffing ratios, supply use, schedule utilization, and service-line performance.
Clarify before posting whether this role owns regional budget variance correction and P&L accountability or supports those functions through senior leadership.

Leadership and Workforce Development

Provide leadership, coaching, and performance accountability for assigned regional clinic managers and operational teams.
Support recruitment, retention, succession planning, leadership development, and workforce optimization.
Promote employee engagement, professional accountability, communication, and AHL culture.
Work with HR and Operations leadership to address vacancies, turnover, performance concerns, and staffing risks.

Key Performance Indicators

Access and Growth: patient growth, new-patient acquisition, third-next-available appointment, template utilization, service line expansion, SBHC utilization, and regional market development.
Quality and Population Health: UDS measures, HEDIS performance, payer quality metrics, preventive screening rates, chronic disease outcomes, health-equity indicators, avoidable ED utilization, and readmission-related measures.
Financial Performance: budget performance, provider productivity, revenue growth, cost management, value-based incentive revenue, and regional operating improvement.
Patient Experience: patient satisfaction, complaint resolution, access metrics, retention, and service recovery.
Workforce: employee engagement, staff retention, vacancy reduction, leadership development, and manager performance.
Community and Growth: new partnerships, referral relationships, community visibility, school district relationships, and implementation of approved regional initiatives.

Decision Authority and Operating Relationships

Authority over assigned regional operations, site performance management, and regional improvement priorities should be defined before posting.
Budget authority, hiring authority, corrective action authority, contract/vendor authority, and approval thresholds should be specified in the final posting or internal offer documentation.
The role should maintain structured operating relationships with Operations, Medical Affairs, Finance, Quality, Population Health, Behavioral Health, Dental, Pharmacy, HR, and Compliance.
The position should not be held accountable for outcomes without access to the operational, financial, clinical, and personnel levers necessary to influence those outcomes.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Public Health, Business Administration, Nursing, or related field.
Minimum of seven years of progressive healthcare leadership experience.
Minimum of five years managing multi-site healthcare operations.
Experience leading population health, quality improvement, value-based care, managed care, or performance improvement initiatives.
Demonstrated success in strategic planning, operational management, community engagement, staff leadership, and performance accountability.
Strong financial, analytical, communication, and operational-management skills.
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel throughout the Northshore region.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Public Health, Business Administration, Nursing, or related field.
FQHC, community health center, integrated care, or safety-net healthcare experience.
Experience with Medicaid managed care, value-based reimbursement, quality incentives, and payer performance metrics.
Knowledge of HRSA, UDS, NCQA, HEDIS, FQHC operations, PPS/APM payment considerations, and healthcare quality reporting.
Experience developing new clinics, programs, partnerships, service lines, or regional growth initiatives.

Core Competencies

Regional leadership and operational accountability.
Strategic planning and disciplined execution.
Population health and value-based care transformation.
Financial stewardship and productivity management.
Data-driven decision making and performance improvement.
Community partnership development and external representation.
Quality improvement, patient experience, and access management.
Workforce leadership, coaching, and change management.
Cross-functional collaboration with clinical and administrative leaders.

Are you a strategic leader who combines expertise in government affairs and health policy with strong communication, collaboration, and organizational skills?

The American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS) is seeking a Director of Government and Political Affairs, Health and Payment Policy to lead the development and implementation of the Society’s policy, advocacy, government relations, and private payer strategies. As a member of the senior management team, this individual will work closely with physician and staff leadership to identify and respond to emerging reimbursement, regulatory, patient safety, and legislative issues at the state and federal levels.

In this role, you’ll guide strategic communications with government agencies, private payers, healthcare organizations, and other key stakeholders while strengthening ASPS’s relationships with national, state, regional, and local partners. About The Port Authority:

Founded in 1921, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey builds, operates, and maintains many of the most important transportation and trade infrastructure assets in the country. The agency's network of aviation, ground, rail, and seaport facilities is among the busiest in the country, supports more than 550,000 regional jobs, and generates more than twenty three billion in annual wages and eighty billion in annual economic activity. The Port Authority also owns and manages the 16-acre World Trade Center site, where the 1,776-foot-tall One World Trade Center is now the tallest skyscraper in the Western Hemisphere.

About The Port Department

The Port Department is one of the five-line department businesses of the PANYNJ. It is responsible for managing the largest port complex on the East Coast and the second largest in the nation. It operates a highly competitive and dynamic business in a very complex political environment. The Port is an economic engine that provides over 580,000 jobs in the region and nearly $240 billion in annual economic activity.

For the past 20 years, the Port has been preparing itself for the growing demand for increased trade resulting in more cargo and for the rapid migration to ever larger vessels. Together with our Port tenants, nearly $15 billion in new infrastructure, equipment and systems has been invested to ensure that Port of New York and New Jersey remains the premier East Coast gateway with even more investment in capacity planned and underway.

As a landlord Port, the Port Authority leases property to tenants that operate Port facilities. Since we do not directly handle cargo, we must influence the efficiency and productivity of the port in more strategic ways. Today, the challenges in this area continue to grow. new_jobs.description:
Waller Consulting post, on behalf of East Coopera Community Outreach

Lead the Next Chapter of Neighbors Helping Neighbors

In 1989, Hurricane Hugo tore through the Lowcountry, and a handful of neighbors turned a parish hall into a lifeline. Thirty-six years later, that same instinct still drives East Cooper Community Outreach (ECCO), a $3.3 million, professionally run nonprofit now serving more than 2,700 individuals a year. After a decade of fast growth, we’re ready to build the fundraising engine and organizational systems to make that growth last. We’re looking for the person who wants to lead that work.

Who We Are 

ECCO provides food, clothing, financial assistance, and dental and medical care to neighbors across Mount Pleasant and East Cooper, paired with coaching and resources (financial workshops, career support, an Asset Development matched-savings program) that help people build lasting stability, not just get through the week. We’ve grown from roughly $500,000 to $3.3 million in annual budget over the last decade, completed a $5.7 million capital campaign, and built a donor base of more than 1,500 people who believe in this work. 
Our culture is the thing people mention first: compassion, collaboration, respect, and integrity, not as a poster on the wall, but as how we actually treat clients, each other, and this community. We’re proud of that, and we’re looking for a CEO who will protect it fiercely while helping us grow.
The Opportunity 

The Board recently elevated this role from Executive Director to CEO, and has built a strong leadership team well positioned to take full responsibility for day-to-day operations, freeing our next CEO to focus on what matters most right now: fundraising, strategy, and building a Board that operates as a true strategic partner. This is a lead-fundraiser role as much as a chief-executive role. Your first job will be strengthening what we’ve already built: stabilizing our development function, deepening donor relationships, and helping our Board grow into stronger governance. From that foundation, you’ll help shape our next 3–5 year strategic plan, including how far and how fast we grow from here. 
Compensation is $128,000 to $160,000, with a comprehensive benefits package including employer-paid health insurance, retirement contributions, and generous paid time off. You’d be doing this work in Mount Pleasant, SC, part of the fast-growing, high-quality-of-life Charleston area. 
A Strong Organization, Ready for What’s Next 

ECCO isn’t a struggling organization looking for someone to rescue it. It’s a 36-year-old institution with real financial momentum (a completed $5.7 million capital campaign, a donor base that keeps growing, three decades of deep community trust), and a culture that clients, staff, and volunteers consistently describe as the best they’ve been part of. That foundation is genuinely rare, and it’s yours to build on, not repair. 
Here’s the honest part: growing organizations outgrow their own systems, and ECCO is right in the middle of that stretch. Our Board is evolving toward stronger strategic governance, our fundraising infrastructure is being built out, and our next CEO will have real influence over how that next chapter takes shape, rather than walking into something already finished. If that sounds like an opportunity instead of a warning sign, keep reading. 
Is This You? 

You’re a real fundraiser.
You’ve personally closed major gifts before, not just supervised someone who did. 
You’re a connector.
You build trust fast with clients, staff, volunteers, donors, and board members alike, and you genuinely like being the face of an organization.
You can manage up.
You know how to set expectations with a board, and you’re energized (not drained) by helping one grow into stronger governance. 
You lead with humility.
Your first instinct in a new role is to listen and learn, not to arrive with a fixed plan; but you’re also ready to lead real change once you’ve earned the trust to do it. 
You’re a builder, not a boss.
You believe in transparent communication, and you want a staff that feels heard, not managed from a distance. 
You think in systems.
You want to help ECCO finish growing up, better systems, better onboarding, better infrastructure, without losing what makes it feel like ECCO.

Support achievement of UDS, HEDIS, payer quality, shared-savings, and value-based incentive opportunities.

Establish a culture of accountability, data-driven management, problem solving, and service excellence.
Review regional quality metrics and coordinate action plans when performance falls below target.

Identify partnerships that improve access, care coordination, community health outcomes, and regional visibility.

Support grant-funded initiatives, sustainability planning, forecasting, and new-service business planning.
